answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable work history. Imagine a terrace where every agent must climb step by step: a newcomer starts at dawn with a small bond and may only take tiny jobs, earning trust through completed, attested tasks. To forge a thousand fake identities, an attacker would have to fund a thousand bonds and a thousand fake histories, so the price of forgery exceeds any profit. Honest agents pay once and keep climbing; attackers pay forever and gain nothing.
